title: Finite-coefficient Frobenius transport commutes with mixed-support cup product
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, integers $a,n\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0$ be a smooth separated finite-type geometrically connected $k_0$-scheme of pure dimension $d\geq0$, let $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and use the small pro-etale derived constant-$A$ module categories of [def-pod-conventions]. Put $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma(z^q)=z$, and $T=Lg^*$. For arbitrary $K,L\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, use the mixed-support cup product $\mu_{K,L}$ of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product] and the transports $\tau_L:R\Gamma(X,L)\to R\Gamma(X,TL)$ and $\tau_{c,K}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\to R\Gamma_c(X,TK)$ of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. Let $b_{K,L}:T(K\otimes_A^L L)\xrightarrow{\sim}TK\otimes_A^L TL$ be the canonical pullback-tensor comparison [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Then the following equality holds in $D(A)$:
$$
 R\Gamma_c(X,b_{K,L})\circ\tau_{c,K\otimes^L L}\circ\mu_{K,L}
 =\mu_{TK,TL}\circ(\tau_{c,K}\otimes_A^L\tau_L).
$$
The same equality holds after shifting either input by any integer, through the canonical tensor and cohomology shift comparisons: in these comparisons $\tau_{L[r]}=\tau_L[r]$ and $\tau_{c,K[r]}=\tau_{c,K}[r]$ for every $r\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Step 1, equivariance of mixed-support cup product, with the finite-coefficient and shift compatibility made explicit; comparison formula also in WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/Derived/WeilFrobenius.lean, isWeilPairing_mixedSupportCupProduct, lines 382-398 (etale version).

proof.text: Write $a=a_X$, $F=La^*$, $R=Ra_*$, $P=Ra_!$, $H=Lg_s^*$ and $T=Lg^*$. Write $e_M:HPM\to PTM$ and $u_M:HRM\to RTM$ for the specified Frobenius exchanges. The Frobenius square is Cartesian with horizontal scheme isomorphisms by [lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian]. It is generally not a square of $k$-morphisms. Work with its underlying ringed topoi throughout. At finite coefficients these pullbacks are exact module inverse images; [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] identifies the horizontal ones with site reindexing equivalences. Thus they preserve bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude: transport a constructible stratification by the isomorphism, and apply the exact tensor equivalence to the defining tensor-vanishing test for amplitude. By [thm-sf-ctf-stability](i)--(iv), $K\otimes^LL$, $PK$, $RL$, $FRL$ and $K\otimes^LFRL$ have the required bounded constructible finite-Tor domains. Set $N=RL$ and let $\theta:FH\xrightarrow{\sim}TF$ be the square comparison. Composition below is right to left and tensors are derived.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text: Choose the base-changed $k_0$-compactification $a=pj$ used in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](2). Its upper Frobenius is denoted $\bar g$. In the notation of [def-exchange-projection], put $B=L\bar g^*$, $J=Lj^*$, $J'=Lj'^*$, $W=Lp^*$, $W'=Lp'^*$ and $S'=Rp'_*$. Then $P=Rp_*j_!$, $e=S'(\beta)\,e_p$, and $\operatorname{PF}_{K,N}=Rp_*(\gamma_{j;K,WN})\,\pi_{p;j_!K,N}$. Primes denote the pulled-back compactification, identified with the same underlying $a$-compactification by the Frobenius isomorphisms. All these are the specified maps, rather than comparisons chosen from invertibility. The finite formulas of [def-exchange-projection] apply over the base scheme $S=s$, viewing $Y'=s$ with structural map $g_s$ and $X'=X$ with structural map $g_s a$. They are finite type over $S$: twisting the scalar action by a field automorphism preserves any finite list of algebra generators. The required arrows are $S$-morphisms by $ag=g_sa$. The underlying sites, coefficient rings and compactification formulas do not depend on these structural labels.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text:
Let $\sigma:TJ\xrightarrow{\sim}J'B$ be the open square comparison and let $b_B,b_T$ denote the pullback-tensor maps. Put $M=j_!K$, $Q=M\otimes WN$, and
$$z=j'_!((1\otimes\sigma_{WN})b_{T;K,JWN})\,\beta_{K\otimes JWN}.$$
The open-factor equality is
$$z\,B(\gamma_{j;K,WN})=\gamma_{j';TK,BWN}(\beta_K\otimes1)b_{B;M,WN}.$$
At each corner the structural ring map is $c^u_A:u^{-1}A\to A$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], which preserves constant sections. This is the finite convention of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus the finite identification clause of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] identifies these $\beta,\gamma$ with the very open maps used in step 2. Indeed [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] identifies $BM$ with $j'_!TK$, and then the source $B(M\otimes WN)$ lies in the fully faithful image of $j'_!$ by the open tensor isomorphism. Restriction by $J'$ determines a map from this image. Both displayed routes restrict to the identity open units followed by the same tensor comparison: this is the restriction normalization of $\beta,\gamma$ in that lemma and the composition and naturality clauses of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Full faithfulness proves the equality. This applies to the semilinear $\bar g$ because the open-normalization statement allows arbitrary scheme maps and ring maps.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text:
Let $\theta_p:W'H\xrightarrow{\sim}BW$ be the proper square comparison, and put $c_Q=(1\otimes\theta_{p,N}^{-1})b_{B;M,WN}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the underlying constant-$A$ ringed-topos square of $p$. Its maps are precisely the proper mate $e_p$ and counit projection $\pi_p$ of step 2, so it gives
$$S'(c_Q)e_{p,Q}H(\pi_{p;M,N})=\pi_{p';BM,HN}(e_{p,M}\otimes1)b_{H;Rp_*M,N}.$$
No $k$-linearity or cartesianness is a hypothesis of that ringed-topos theorem. Thus it applies to this Frobenius square without a change of coefficient categories.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text:
Expand $\operatorname{PF}=Rp_*(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ and $e=S'(\beta)e_p$ in the left route of the projection square. Naturality of $e_p$ moves $H(Rp_*\gamma_j)$ past $e_p$. The open identity of step 3 then replaces $zB\gamma_j$ by $\gamma_{j'}(\beta_K\otimes1)b_B$. Move $\theta_{p,N}^{-1}$ through $\gamma_{j'}$ by its naturality and apply the proper identity of step 4. Finally naturality of $\pi_{p'}$ moves $S'(\beta_K)$ to its first input. The resulting equality, with $\theta:FH\cong TF$, is
$$P(c_{K,N})e_{K\otimes FN}H(\operatorname{PF}_{K,N})
=\operatorname{PF}_{TK,HN}(e_K\otimes1)b_{H;PK,N},
\qquad c_{K,N}=(1\otimes\theta_N^{-1})b_{T;K,FN}.$$
The target comparison is $T(K\otimes FN)\to TK\otimes FHN$; the pullback-composition clause in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] identifies it with the composite through $z$ and $J'(\theta_{p,N}^{-1})$. This proves the needed projection square by its actual proper and open factors; it does not assume that the $k$-linear base-change statement applies to $g_s$.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text:
The defining mate formula for $u_L$ in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange](1) says exactly
$$\varepsilon_{TL}\,F(u_L)=T(\varepsilon_L)\,\theta_{RL}:FHRL\longrightarrow TL.$$
Consequently, by tensor functoriality and naturality of $b_T$,
$$b_{T;K,L}\,T(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)
=(1_{TK}\otimes\varepsilon_{TL})(1_{TK}\otimes F(u_L))c_{K,RL}.$$
This is the counit comparison needed for the second arrow of cup product; it follows from the transpose defining this particular ordinary exchange.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text:
Before applying the point functor write $m_{K,L}=P(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)\operatorname{PF}_{K,RL}$, the map defining mixed-support cup product. Naturality of $e$ at $1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L$, followed by step 6 and then step 5 at $N=RL$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
P(b_{T;K,L})e_{K\otimes L}H(m_{K,L})
&=P(1\otimes\varepsilon_{TL})P(1\otimes F(u_L))
\operatorname{PF}_{TK,HRL}(e_K\otimes1)b_{H;PK,RL}\\
&=m_{TK,TL}(e_K\otimes u_L)b_{H;PK,RL}.
\end{aligned}$$
For the second equality, use naturality of $\operatorname{PF}$ in its second variable at $u_L:HRL\to RTL$; tensor bifunctoriality gives $(1\otimes u_L)(e_K\otimes1)=e_K\otimes u_L$. The cited definitions explicitly make these maps composites of natural transformations. This establishes cup equivariance in $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ for arbitrary $K,L$, without Weil data on either input.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text:
Put $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$. Under the canonical tensor identification of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], the finite point transport satisfies
$$V(b_{H;U,W})\,\iota_{U\otimes W}=\iota_U\otimes\iota_W.$$
To check this, use the exact section functor and the restriction--insertion--$x\mapsto x\otimes1$ formula of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. On a pure tensor of sections in degrees $i,j$, the route on the left restricts $x\otimes y$ along $g_s$, inserts it and applies tensor comparison; the right route restricts and inserts $x,y$ separately and tensors their images. Both are $(\operatorname{res}_{g_s}x\otimes1)\otimes(\operatorname{res}_{g_s}y\otimes1)$. The insertion and sheafification maps respect these tensor relations by construction of sheaf tensor. Apply this calculation to K-flat flat-term models: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] gives those tensor models and preservation of K-flatness under pullback; the point tensor is the canonical comparison on them. Additivity gives equality on the total complexes and localization gives the displayed derived identity.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text:
Apply $V$ to step 7 and precompose with $\iota_{PK\otimes RL}$. Naturality of point transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), at $m_{K,L}$, replaces $V(Hm)\iota_{PK\otimes RL}$ by $\iota_{P(K\otimes L)}V(m)$. Step 8 replaces the tensor comparison followed by point transport by $\iota_{PK}\otimes\iota_{RL}$. Since [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport] defines $\tau_{c,M}=V(e_M)\iota_{PM}$ and $\tau_M=V(u_M)\iota_{RM}$, the resulting equality is precisely
$$R\Gamma_c(X,b_{K,L})\,\tau_{c,K\otimes L}\,\mu_{K,L}
=\mu_{TK,TL}(\tau_{c,K}\otimes\tau_L).$$
All tensor identifications used in applying $V$ are natural by [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor].

proof.text: For an integer $r$, the unit and counit of every derived pullback/direct-image adjunction in the mate formulas commute with $[r]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]. The finite pullbacks are termwise exact inverse images; their composition and square comparisons commute with shift because they act in each degree by the same module map. Thus their unit--square--counit composite $u_{L[r]}$ is $u_L[r]$ through the composite shift comparisons. For compact support, the proper exchange has the same property, while the open $\beta$ has it too: restrict to the open, where it is the identity by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and use full faithfulness. Whiskering by the exact termwise $j_!$ and derived $Rp_*$ preserves these equalities. Hence $e_{K[r]}=e_K[r]$. This uses the fixed compactification of the definition, so no extra independence or comparison theorem is needed. Here $\beta$ is the fixed-constant-section map identified in step 3.

source.place: Step 1: mixed-support cup equivariance, expanded at finite coefficients

proof.text: The cup map itself respects the same separate shifts. Expand it as $P(1\otimes\varepsilon_L)Rp_*(\gamma_j)\pi_p$ as in steps 2 and 7. For a shift in $L$, the ordinary counit commutes with shift by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift], and the second-variable projection comparison does so by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. For a shift in $K$, the proper projection is the mate of $(\varepsilon_{j_!K}\otimes1)b_W$; its unit and counit commute with shift by the same derived-adjunction statement, and $b_W$ does so by the pullback-tensor shift clause of the projection-mate statement. The open $\gamma_j$ commutes with either shift: after restricting to the open, it is the identity tensor identification, so full faithfulness in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] proves this assertion. Whiskering and composition give the assertion for the displayed cup composite. These calculations use exactly the signed total-tensor comparisons, and apply to every integer shift. The $\gamma_j$ used here is the same fixed-scalar finite map identified in step 3.

source.place: Steps 1--2, canonical shifts of the finite cup composite

proof.text: The restriction, insertion and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ maps defining $\iota$ are degree-zero maps of complexes, so their map on a shifted complex is their shifted map. Together with steps 10--11 and the definition of $\tau$ this proves $\tau_{L[r]}=\tau_L[r]$ and $\tau_{c,K[r]}=\tau_{c,K}[r]$ for every integer $r$. Apply steps 1--9 to $K[r],L$ and to $K,L[r]$; these are still arbitrary bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs. Read the equalities through the canonical cochain shifts. In the second tensor variable the comparison on a summand of first-factor degree $i$ has sign $(-1)^{ri}$; the same sign occurs on both routes since all transports have degree zero. In the first variable its standard comparison has no extra sign. These comparisons commute with $b_T$ by the shift clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Thus the stated shifted equalities and both asserted transport identifications hold, including negative shifts.

Step 3 checks this through c^u_A, using def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom and prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, which allows any scheme morphism, including the semilinear g-bar. Steps 10-11 reuse the same beta and gamma. Repaired. Steps 4-7: I recomputed the pasting myself. The proper factor comes from lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence, which needs no k-linearity or Cartesian square; its pi and Ex are exactly the maps of def-exchange-projection. The open factor follows from full faithfulness and identity restriction. Step 6 is the counit transpose of the u_L definition. Step 7 uses naturality of PF in its second variable at u_L, with second input RL. Step 8: the point tensor is canonical in the sense of def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-finite-models, and the generator computation holds. Step 9: point-transport naturality at m_{K,L} gives exactly the displayed equality. Steps 10-12: shifts follow from lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact, with matching signs on both routes.
